exactText: I am no longer confident that PCE inflation will move back to 2% in the next year or two without the Fed raising interest rates.
sourceQuote: I am no longer confident that PCE inflation will move back to 2% in the next year or two without the Fed raising interest rates.
normalizedClaim: Without additional Fed rate hikes, PCE inflation is unlikely to return to 2% within the next one to two years.
resolutionCriteria: Core or headline PCE remaining above 2% through September 2028 if the Fed does not hike from the September 2026 level.

exactText: I view a modest increase in the funds rate, starting with a quarter point in September and maybe 50 or 75 basis points higher in total by the end of the year, as a way to ensure inflation is trending down in a timely way.
sourceQuote: a modest increase in the funds rate, starting with a quarter point in September and maybe 50 or 75 basis points higher in total by the end of the year
normalizedClaim: A modest Fed funds rate increase of 25–75 basis points in the remainder of 2026 is appropriate to bring inflation down.
resolutionCriteria: Federal funds rate path in late 2026 including at least one 25 bp hike, with total tightening up to 75 bp by year-end.

exactText: Sahm indicated that a recession is unlikely in the near term.
sourceQuote: a recession is unlikely in the near term.
normalizedClaim: A U.S. recession is unlikely in the near term as of mid-2026.
resolutionCriteria: No NBER-dated recession beginning in the second half of 2026 or early 2027.

exactText: the United States may have just had a year with essentially no net job growth, yet without being in a recession.
sourceQuote: a year with essentially no net job growth, yet without being in a recession.
normalizedClaim: 2025 featured essentially zero net job growth without constituting a recession.
resolutionCriteria: BLS payroll data for 2025 showing near-zero net employment change and absence of NBER recession dating for that period.

resolution.explanation: Subsequent data and Sahm’s own follow-up confirmed stalled payroll growth without a recession.

evidence.sourceTitle: BLS Employment Situation and Sahm Substack update

exactText: Soft landing: inflation to 2%, unemployment low (no recession).
sourceQuote: Soft landing: inflation to 2%, unemployment low (no recession).
normalizedClaim: A soft landing is defined as inflation returning to 2% with low unemployment and no recession.
resolutionCriteria: Whether 2024–2026 outcomes match this definition of soft landing.

exactText: the primary risk at present is inflation rather than economic stagnation.
sourceQuote: the primary risk at present is inflation rather than economic stagnation.
normalizedClaim: As of mid-2026 the dominant macroeconomic risk is inflation, not stagnation or recession.
resolutionCriteria: Inflation remaining the more binding constraint on policy relative to unemployment or growth through late 2026.

exactText: Before the March meeting, I was still looking for cuts this year; by June, I had moved to a hold; now I see a couple of hikes and a higher path in the years beyond.
sourceQuote: now I see a couple of hikes and a higher path in the years beyond.
normalizedClaim: The appropriate policy path shifted to include rate hikes in 2026 and a higher funds rate trajectory thereafter.
resolutionCriteria: Fed policy actions and SEP projections reflecting higher rates than those anticipated in early 2026.

exactText: At present, she does not see that recessionary pattern.
sourceQuote: At present, she does not see that recessionary pattern.
normalizedClaim: The Sahm Rule recession indicator is not currently signaling a recession as of mid-2026.
resolutionCriteria: Real-time Sahm Rule value remaining below the 0.50 threshold through at least late 2026.

resolution.explanation: FRED real-time Sahm Rule remained well below 0.50 in mid-to-late 2026.

evidence.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis

exactText: The Fed’s rate decision should reflect a wide range of data. The date of the election is not one of them.
sourceQuote: The date of the election is not one of them.
normalizedClaim: Federal Reserve rate decisions should ignore the electoral calendar and be based solely on economic data and outlook.
resolutionCriteria: Observable Fed behavior and communications treating election timing as non-decisive through the 2026 cycle.

exactText: this is simply what a soft landing looks like—slowing employment growth without a sharp contraction in activity.
sourceQuote: slowing employment growth without a sharp contraction in activity.
normalizedClaim: The observed pattern of stalled job growth alongside continued economic expansion constitutes a form of soft landing.
resolutionCriteria: Continuation of positive GDP growth concurrent with weak or zero employment growth without tipping into recession in 2025–2026.
